newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP demands changes to designation of origin scheme.
newsitem.headline: EP demands changes to designation of origin scheme.

text.p: The European Parliament called on Friday for changes to European Commission plans to amend EU legislation on regional products like feta cheese and Cornish pasties.
Regulation EEC/2081/92, introduced in 1992, is designed to promote sales of regional farm products by assigning them a designation of origin which is a guarantee of their quality.
The sheer volume of applications for registration, over 1,500, led to huge delays with the new five-year scheme so the Commission is now proposing to extend it.
Under the proposal, COM(96)266, products could benefit from the scheme for five years from the date of registration, rather than from the date the law first came into force.
But parliament said that introducing a staggered time period for products would lead to confusion, affect global sales and undermine the credibility of the regulation.
Euro-MPs adopted an amendment to the proposal which says the regulation should continue to apply, as before, from 1992, but should be extended from five to seven years.
Another amendment says national designations should be allowed to apply until an EU registration is granted.
Parliament also called for a deadline for introducing an EU designation.
